title: KMS Egress, Billing, and Legal Handshake
next_steps: Redwood: Send redlined DPA + short summary of redline rationale (by 2025-05-01)
SE: Schedule 2-hour technical benchmark (model + egress profile) w/ Sable infra team (by 2025-05-05)
Legal: Align on KMS/HSM options and preferred key management pattern (customer to confirm by 2025-05-08)
Redwood: Provide pricing scenarios including egress-by-region and dedicated-reserved commits (by 2025-05-02)
action_items: Alex Moreno - email DPA redline and SOC 2 report link - 2025-05-01
Priya Desai - scope benchmark runbook and test script - 2025-05-03
Ibrahim Saleh - share VPC peering and egress baseline (cloud regions) - 2025-05-02
June Park - send list of absolute must-have legal clauses re: data residency & escrow - 2025-05-04
meeting_header: Date: 2025-04-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Redwood AE+SE+CSM, Sable Financial procurement/legal/security/finops
summary: Kickoff handshake between Redwood and Sable Financial to align on DPA redlines, KMS options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), and how egress billing will be modeled across regions. Main blockers: legal wants stronger key custody language and escrow/indemnity clarifications; finops needs transparent egress scenarios; security asked about on-prem HSM path for Private deployment.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're, uh, Alex from Redwood. quick roll call?
[00:06] Mark (Procurement): Mark here, June from legal, Ibrahim security, Tara finops.
[00:12] Priya (SE): Priya on my side, I'll run the technical asks later in the call.
[00:18] Alex: Cool, objective today is to get alignment on the DPA redlines, KMS/egress expectations and next steps so procurement can map timelines.
[00:30] June (Legal): Right, we reviewed the DPA. overall good, but two sticking points: key custody language and indemnity around data exfil. we also want clarity on data residency egress fees, like if data leaves eu region to us, who bears that?
[00:45] Alex: totally. on keys we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. for private deployments we can integrate with your HSM, that path has extra paperwork but it's doable.
[00:58] Ibrahim (Security): quick clarification, when you say integrate with our HSM, do you mean full key custody lives on our side and Redwood never sees the unwrapped key? that's a must for some regs.
[01:10] Priya: yes, the private/onprem path uses a customer keywrap model — Redwood holds only encrypted material, key material stays in HSM. there's an operational playbook, and we can share a diagram. sometimes the transcript from the ops docs calls it "key wrap" or K V catch uh kv cache, which is confusing in auto notes.
[01:30] Tara (FinOps): On egress billing, we need scenarios. Our cloud costs spike if model inferences route to a different cloud region. we need per-region egress rates and an example invoice.
[01:42] Alex: understood. We'll produce 3 scenarios: hosted with multi-region fallback, dedicated-reserved in single region, and private/VPC w/ local egress. each will show token cost + egress cost assumptions.
[01:55] June: Also legal asked for an escrow mention — in the event of bankruptcy we need source release or a plan for continuity. is that something Redwood has a standard for?
[02:08] Alex: we have an escrow option (third-party escrow) used for enterprise; I'll attach the clause we've used before. want to be clear: it's negotiable but we can provide a standard template.
[02:20] Mark: timeline wise procurement wants pricing approved by May 12 to hit June go/no-go. is that feasible?
[02:28] Alex: short answer yes if legal and finops get the redlines and scenarios this week. we'll prioritize.
[02:34] Ibrahim: security deep dive - what about audit logs and KMS audit trails? we need proof of key rotation, access logs, and CloudHSM integration details.
[02:46] Priya: we can provide audit log exports (s3 dump or syslog), and KMS events are surfaced via our control plane and also can forward to your SIEM. rotation patterns depend on the KMS you select — if it's customer KMS we defer to your rotation.
[03:02] Tara: another question: if we use dedicated reserved capacity, do egress costs change? we assume not, but want a break down per token + network.
[03:12] Alex: egress is network-level and billed separately; dedicated capacity affects compute unit pricing but not inter-region transfer fees. however we can offer a committed egress discount in the contract if you commit to X TB/month
[03:25] June: Commercially, our counsel wants a cap on egress-related pass-through charges, or at least an example cost cap.
[03:33] Alex: we can propose a tiered cap tied to commit bands; we'll show that in the pricing scenarios doc.
[03:40] Ibrahim: one more security nuance — permanent log retention of prompts vs ephemeral. we need write/read controls and the ability to opt-out retention.
[03:50] Priya: Redwood supports configurable retention per-route; for private deployments you can set zero retention. Hosted default is 30 days but that's configurable in enterprise plan. we'll include the retention controls doc.
[04:05] Mark: ok good. June, anything else on legal?
[04:08] June: liability limits — the customer needs reasonable liability carve-outs for data breaches caused by third-party cloud providers. also, we want SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning to be spelled out.
[04:20] Alex: SAML/SCIM supported, and we can add the SSO handoff flow. on liability, we usually keep standard caps, but we can add carve-outs for third-party cloud breaches; we'll tee up language.
[04:34] Tara: re billing cadence, we prefer monthly with line-item for egress by region. is that standard?
[04:41] Olivia (CSM): yes monthly billing is standard. we can produce a sample invoice that splits compute vs egress vs support/entitlements.
[04:49] Mark: procurement is also asking about subprocessor list and whether Redwood uses any cross-border subprocessors that store data in a different jurisdiction.
[04:58] Alex: we'll share the current subprocessor list and our certs; for any changes we provide notice windows.
[05:06] June: on the DPA we proposed a few redlines around deletion proofs and audit rights. expect to see those in our email.
[05:14] Alex: great. I'll coordinate with Priya to attach the SOC 2 plus the private deployment HSM integration doc.
[05:20] Priya: for the benchmark, we'll want a sample prompt set and representative traffic shapes (burst, steady-state, long-context). Ibrahim, can you share network egress baselines so we can simulate costs?
[05:33] Ibrahim: yes, I'll pull last quarter of region egress in CSV.
[05:36] Alex: Perfect. Recap: Redwood sends DPA redline + SOC2 + pricing scenarios + escrow clause; SE schedules benchmark and sends runbook; Customer to send legal must-haves and egress numbers.
[05:50] Mark: one last thing — are there competitors on your side we should be aware of? we've had ProviderX in parallel procurement.
[05:58] Alex: noted. we're comfortable competing on the end-to-end private options and transparency on egress.
[06:05] June: ok that's all. thanks all.
[06:09] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the technical run.
[06:15] [call ends]
notes: Customer emphasized need for customer-managed KMS and HSM integration for regs.
FinOps requires concrete egress pricing scenarios and a sample invoice.
Legal will circulate redlines focused on deletion proofs, audit rights, and escrow/source release.
SE to run benchmark with customer-provided egress numbers; timeline target early May.
